events.label: Trump to Axios: 'big decision' on resuming strikes
events.description: In a Thursday Axios interview Trump said he faces a 'big decision' on whether to resume large-scale attacks on Iran and 'annihilate' its government ('Anything could happen with me'). He gave no timeline, said Tehran was still in contact and wanted a deal, and said he would first hear from the GCC states on the UNGA sidelines the next Tuesday. Axios also reported that Trump and Hegseth had told the military to hold Middle East force levels through year-end.

events.label: IRGC claims strike on tanker Trend
events.description: The IRGC Navy said it hit the Togo-flagged tanker Trend, which caught fire and stopped, during an 'illegal passage' of Hormuz after being 'provoked and deceived' by the US military, and warned that such ships face destruction. UKMTO reported an attack on the Omani side of the strait without naming the vessel, and there is no independent confirmation. Date corrected from the candidate's Sep 18: Reuters carried the claim on Sep 17.

events.label: Fox poll: 60% say war wrong, 71% see no plan
events.description: Fox News poll (1,211 registered voters, Sep 11-14), published Sep 17: 60% say military action against Iran was the wrong decision and 37% right. 71% say the administration lacks a plan to end the war, including 43% of Republicans. Trump's overall job approval is 39/61.

events.label: Trump at UN: deal or 'annihilate' Iran
events.description: Trump's UNGA address (Tue Sep 22), about 40 minutes and largely a defence of the war, framed a choice between a deal that lets Iran rebuild and quickly 'annihilating' the Islamic Republic. He said a deal could come after the midterms and that the two sides would 'get it done, one way or the other'. Iran's delegation walked out. The meeting with GCC leaders on the sidelines had been set for the same day (Axios); no outcome was confirmed.

events.label: Araghchi meets Witkoff, Kushner at the UN
events.description: Hours after Trump's speech, FM Araghchi met envoys Witkoff and Kushner on the UNGA sidelines, at the US side's request according to Iranian state TV. Trump said the session lasted about three hours, called it productive, and said another round would come 'in the very near future'. Accounts differ on whether the two sides met directly: the NYT, citing Iranian officials, said Pakistan and Qatar mediated. Iran set out its terms for reopening Hormuz: lift the naval blockade, release frozen assets, and end the war on all 'resistance' fronts.

events.label: Pezeshkian at UN: Iran 'ready for dialogue', won't bow
events.description: A day after Trump's 'annihilate' threat, President Pezeshkian gave a rare wartime UNGA speech. He said Iranians were the 'victims of terrorism' and held up images of the dead, including Ali Khamenei and the Minab schoolchildren. He told 'Mr. Trump and those who seek to bully us' that Iran is ready for negotiations 'without accepting the language of force'. The lone US delegate in the hall walked out.

events.label: Bulk carrier Cape Dao hit; Indian sailor killed
events.description: The Antigua and Barbuda-flagged bulk carrier Cape Dao was hit about 2.5 nm off Oman's Musandam; UKMTO said by an unknown projectile, while one outlet reported torpedoes. One Indian crew member was killed and Oman's navy rescued the rest; the ship was left burning and adrift. No one claimed the attack.

events.label: Senate rejects war powers 49-50; Tillis flips
events.description: The Senate voted 49-50 (Thu Sep 24) against the House-passed resolution to remove US forces from hostilities with Iran. Paul, Collins and Murkowski voted yes, joined for the first time by Tillis (after 12 'no' votes), who cited 60 days since the administration told Congress in July that 'military action' had restarted. Fetterman voted no and Alsobrooks did not vote.

events.label: Carlson on NPR: Trump said 'we'll all die anyway'
events.description: In an NPR Newsmakers interview with Steve Inskeep, Tucker Carlson said that when he warned Trump in the Oval Office days before the war, Trump answered 'we'll all die anyway' (also quoted as 'we all die anyway'). Carlson called it nihilism and blamed Israel for pushing the war. The quote rests on Carlson's account alone. The White House did not address it and sent a Trump post calling Carlson and others 'stupid people'.

events.label: Cohen files 26 impeachment articles, one on Iran
events.description: Retiring Rep. Steve Cohen (D-Tenn.) introduced 26 articles of impeachment against Trump. Article II charges abuse of power for waging war on Iran without congressional approval. Cohen acknowledged the resolution will not advance.

events.label: Trump rejects Iran's seven-day plan
events.description: Leaving the White House on Saturday Sep 26, Trump said Iran's seven-day plan 'would not be acceptable' and that Iran wants the strait opened 'because they're losing so badly'. Under the plan the US would lift the blockade, waive oil sanctions, release about $12bn in frozen assets and observe a wider ceasefire including Lebanon and Yemen; Iran would then reopen Hormuz and begin final-deal talks. He also shared a map labelling the waterway the 'Trump Strait'. A report cited by Fox said he told aides he expects strikes to resume after the midterms.

events.label: IRGC open letter urges US voters to reject Trump
events.description: IRGC spokesman Hossein Mohebbi released an open letter 'to the American people' (25 or 26 pages; reports differ) urging voters to reject Trump's policies at the midterms. He said it was aimed at voters, not the administration. On Sep 30 a State Department spokesperson called it 'nothing more than a smokescreen'.

events.label: Qatar relays messages; Iran gets US reply on 7-day plan
events.description: Qatari foreign ministry spokesman Majed Al-Ansari said on Tuesday Sep 29 that Doha is 'currently relaying messages between the American and Iranian sides'. One candidate dated this Oct 6, but Anadolu published it Sep 29. On Sep 30 Reuters reported that Araghchi had received Washington's feedback on Iran's seven-day trust-building plan from Qatari mediators in Doha. The dispute is over the order of steps, not the plan's content, despite Trump's public rejection.

events.label: Trump video: Iran 'crazy', 'maybe you blow them up'
events.description: In a Truth Social video post (9:36 PM EDT Sep 30) Trump calls Iran's leaders 'crazy' and irrational and asks how a deal can be made with them. 'Maybe you blow them up': the choice is to 'blow them up, make a deal', and it will end 'very soon one way or the other'.

events.label: ~9,000 troops, third carrier head to Mideast
events.description: AP reported on Thursday Oct 1 that about 9,000 US personnel were heading to the Middle East with the USS Theodore Roosevelt carrier group, which left San Diego, and the USS Makin Island amphibious ready group, as Trump weighs new strikes. He called a post-election bombing ramp-up 'possible'. A US official said the Roosevelt is due by the end of November, not October as one candidate had it.

events.label: AP-NORC: 69% say war not worth fighting
events.description: AP-NORC poll of more than 2,000 adults, released Thursday Oct 1: 69% say the Iran war has not been worth fighting, up five points since July, and 71% disapprove of Trump's handling of Iran.

events.label: Tanker attacks hit a weekly record
events.description: CNBC (Oct 9) counted 11 tankers attacked in Hormuz in the week ending Oct 4, the most strikes on commercial ships since the war began. Another analysis counted a dozen ships attacked Oct 5-11, also a weekly high. Reuters, citing a think tank, called October the worst month yet for ship attacks. The date marks the end of the record week, not a single incident.

events.label: Trump: 'Let them take out Los Angeles'
events.description: At a midterm rally in Grand Island, Nebraska, Trump said of Iran: 'Let them take out Los Angeles. Let them take out San Diego. This is a very small price to pay.' Newsom called him 'deranged and dangerous', LA Mayor Bass objected, and the backlash crossed party lines. The White House said the remark was taken out of context and that he meant a nuclear Iran could strike US cities.

events.label: Vance: Iran must cut enrichment to end war
events.description: In a Reuters interview given Monday Oct 5 in Fairbanks and published Oct 6, Vance said any deal needs a 'meaningful' reduction in Iran's enrichment capacity, not assurances: 'If you don't want a nuclear weapon, then why do you need 60% enriched fuel?' He said it is unclear how much authority Iran's negotiators hold. A senior Iranian official replied that recognition of Iran's right to enrich is Tehran's red line.

events.label: Trump: no attack on Iran before midterms
events.description: On Thursday Oct 8 Trump posted on Truth Social that 'we will not be attacking Iran at any time prior to the Midterm Elections' (Nov 3), citing 'productive discussions' with Iran. The blockade and sanctions stay. It followed an Atlantic report that the White House had asked the Pentagon for strike options usable before the vote, and an oil-price surge. It frames the rest of the window as a pre-midterm hold: there have been no US strikes on Iran since early September.

events.label: Treasury sanctions 17 shadow-fleet tankers
events.description: Under Operation Economic Outcast, Treasury sanctioned 17 vessels in Iran's shadow fleet on Oct 8, saying this neutralizes most of what remains of the network. A same-day State Department action added entities, individuals and five vessels; Iran International put the total at 22 vessels.

events.label: Pew: 65% disapprove; GOP approval slips to 63%
events.description: Pew survey (Sep 28-Oct 4, 5,062 adults), published Oct 8: 65% disapprove of Trump's handling of the Iran military action and 33% approve. 34% say the decision to use force was right, down 4 points from March. Republican approval is 63%, down from 69% in March. 47% expect the war to last more than another year.

events.label: Carlson calls the war 'treason'; WH: 'whiny turncoat'
events.description: Tucker Carlson told Arabian Business that Trump's 'voluntary, ruinous' war with Iran amounts to treason against the US. A White House spokesman did not dispute his account, restated that Iran will never get a nuclear weapon, and called Carlson 'a whiny turncoat who dramatically overestimates his influence and relevance'. The search reported the article as dated Oct 8; the page itself was not opened.

events.label: Houthi missile hits Riyadh airport, 12-13 killed
events.description: A Houthi missile struck King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh on Saturday Oct 10. Saudi authorities first said 12 were killed and 309 injured; later reports say at least 13, the deadliest attack on Saudi soil in over a decade. An Oct 8 strike had killed three, and Riyadh was targeted again on Oct 11-12. The US later ordered non-emergency staff out of Saudi Arabia.

events.label: Container ship GFS Pride sunk near Hormuz
events.description: The Singapore-flagged container ship GFS Pride was hit on Oct 13, caught fire and had sunk by Oct 14. Singapore's MPA said all 21 crew were evacuated; CNN reported one death, unconfirmed elsewhere. Singapore cited an unidentified projectile; the IRGC said the ship hit a naval mine. Its sister ship GFS Giselle was damaged. The IMO counts it as the third commercial ship sunk in the war. CNN tied the surge in attacks to the midterms.

events.label: Trump: 'should have probably left their leaders'
events.description: At a Wednesday-night rally in Kalispell, Montana, for House candidate Aaron Flint, Trump said Iran has no navy or air force and its leaders are gone, then added: 'I should have probably left their leaders because I don't know who the hell we're negotiating with.' He said Iran's main ask in talks is 'Will you please allow us to live?'. The Iran International post decodes to Oct 15 03:36 UTC, which is Oct 14 evening US time.

events.label: Trump rules out nukes; MOAB strike plans reported
events.description: To Newsmax (Oct 15) Trump said 'I wouldn't use nuclear, we don't have to', called the 'mother of all bombs' conventional, and on ground troops for a Pickaxe Mountain strike said 'No, I don't see that.' The same day CNN reported new US strike plans, including possible MOAB use, against Iranian energy and nuclear sites. Bloomberg said he declined to rule out using the MOAB after the midterms.

events.label: Polls: war a top midterm issue; FP approval lows
events.description: Fox News poll (Oct 9-12, 1,202 RV): 75% extremely or very concerned about the war, six in ten oppose military action, and Trump's foreign policy approval is 35%, Fox's lowest of his second term. AP-NORC (Oct 8-12): 62% of registered voters call the war one of the most important issues, and foreign policy approval is 33%, the low across eight polls this term. The date is the Responsible Statecraft roundup (Oct 16); the two polls' release days were not seen.

events.label: Pakistan suspends trade at Iran border crossings
events.description: Pakistan's Commerce Ministry withdrew its Oct 3 order allowing trade through the Taftan and Gabd-Rimdan crossings, citing security and smuggling. Commercial traffic stopped from Oct 17 while passenger traffic continued. Iran said the border stayed open, and trade only partly resumed by Oct 26.

events.label: Vance: 'in some ways we have won decisively'
events.description: At a CBS News 'Things That Matter' town hall in Michigan that aired Saturday evening (Oct 17), Tony Dokoupil asked why the US hasn't decisively won. Vance said 'in some ways we have won decisively' but 'the enemy gets a vote here'. A man whose wife died in an Iranian strike pressed him on 'fundamental failures'.

events.label: Hegseth meets Netanyahu in unannounced visit
events.description: Hegseth met Netanyahu and Defense Minister Katz at Ovda Air Base during an unannounced visit, first reported by Axios, eight days before Israel's election. Iran dominated the talks, which came amid US-Israeli discussion of resuming major combat. Hegseth said only that he visited troops and spoke with the prime minister. Some outlets date it Oct 20, but Hegseth confirmed Oct 19.

events.label: Rezaei: no uranium leaves Iran; Netanyahu vows regime's end
events.description: SNSC secretary Mohsen Rezaei told visiting Pakistani army chief Asim Munir that Iran will not hand over enriched uranium under any deal and will not negotiate until the US builds trust; Speaker Ghalibaf echoed him. The same day Netanyahu said at Kiryat Shmona, 'We must complete the elimination of the Iranian regime — that is the primary objective.'

events.label: Rubio: Iran using 'Nazi U-boat tactics'
events.description: In an interview with India's News18 during a Mumbai visit, Rubio said Iran is targeting merchant ships and trying to kill civilian sailors with Nazi U-boat-style tactics. He said a deal is hard with 'radical Shia clerics' in charge and promised 'extraordinary economic pressure', while claiming Hormuz traffic was back to 80-100% of prewar levels.

events.label: Reports: Trump blocked Israeli strike; post-midterm plan
events.description: Two reports on Oct 21. The FT, citing three sources, said Israel had prepared a multi-day campaign against Iranian nuclear, power and regime targets, aimed at around the weekend of Oct 10, which Trump opposed before the midterms; Netanyahu called the report 'biased and untrue'. The NYT said the US and Israel had drawn up plans for a 'short but intensive' operation after Nov 3, possibly including Pickaxe Mountain. The White House did not comment on plans 'that may or may not exist'.

events.label: MTG: attack Iran and El-Sayed wins Michigan
events.description: Marjorie Taylor Greene posted on X (Oct 21, 21:40 UTC, from @FmrRepMTG): 'If Trump is dumb enough to attack Iran again before the midterms, @AbdulElSayed will win the senate seat in Michigan. It's a stupid senseless war and America hates it.' She said it was not an endorsement.

events.label: Trump: 'not negotiating'; calls ship-hit claims fake
events.description: Asked by NewsNation (reported late Oct 21 to Oct 22, US time) whether he was done negotiating, Trump said talks were happening 'a little bit', then 'I think we're not negotiating', that something will happen 'fairly soon', and that 'most people seem to think it's after the election.' On Oct 22 the IRGC claimed it had set four ship-to-ship tankers on fire in the northern Gulf and that three more had hit mines west of Hormuz. CENTCOM called the mine claims false. In a Truth Social post at 11:40 AM EDT, Trump accused Iran of making up attacks and mines to drive up oil before the midterms.

events.label: Trump: 'We may do another little Epic Fury'
events.description: At a Friday rally in Fort Myers, Florida, Trump said 'We may do another little Epic Fury, or they'll agree.' The same day, envoy Tom Barrack told Mario Nawfal that a US strike could come as soon as that weekend; Trump said he knew nothing about it.

events.label: DNI memo: Iranian plots in 'advanced stages'
events.description: An unclassified memo from DNI Jay Clayton to Rubio, dated Oct 23 and first reported by Axios (dated Oct 24), warns that Iranian lethal plots against US officials have reached 'advanced stages'. State ordered non-emergency staff out of the Riyadh embassy and its consulates; reports date that order Oct 21-23, and the public announcement cited Houthi threats.

events.label: European, Mideast FMs meet in Istanbul on Hormuz
events.description: Turkey's FM Fidan hosted the foreign ministers of Britain, France, Germany and Italy with Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Egypt, the first meeting in this format. They urged restraint and diplomacy, the reopening of Hormuz and an end to Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia. Fidan said military intervention is not a solution.

events.label: Alex Jones: Trump wrong on Iran, vote GOP anyway
events.description: Alex Jones on X (status decodes to Oct 23 17:24 UTC): 'Yes Trump Was Wrong To Start The Iran War, But We Must Live In Reality And We Cannot Flush Our Country Down The Toilet And Let The Democrat Socialists Win. Vote For Your Local Republicans!' He called for impeachment in July, so this marks an anti-war MAGA account closing ranks before the vote. @RealAlexJones is a tracked account.

events.label: Trump: 'deal or finish them off?'; Qatari draft
events.description: On Fox's Sunday Morning Futures (Oct 25) Trump asked 'Do I make a deal with them or do I finish them off?' ('Getting to be decision time') and said there would be no strike that day. Per an official briefed on the talks (Reuters, reported Oct 28), Qatari mediators gave Iran a new draft that day: daily reciprocal steps over seven days, with guarantor states. A senior Iranian official called it 'unacceptable ideas and not an offer'.

events.label: Mecca Pact envoys in Tehran to avert renewed war
events.description: Saudi Defence Minister Khalid bin Salman, Pakistan's Field Marshal Asim Munir and Turkish intelligence chief Ibrahim Kalin met Pezeshkian and Rezaei in Tehran on Monday Oct 26. They came as members of the Mecca (Makkah) Joint Defence Agreement, to de-escalate between Iran and the US and over the Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia. Iran International called it a possible 'last chance' before military action. No agreement was announced.

events.label: Israel election: neither bloc reaches 61
events.description: Final count of the Oct 27 Knesset election: Netanyahu's bloc 53 seats, the Eisenkot-led bloc 48, Arab parties 19. Neither side can form a government without the other or the Arab parties, so Netanyahu stays on as caretaker during coalition talks. Turnout was 77.9%.

events.label: Pope: 'There is no such thing as a holy war'
events.description: Recovering from his Oct 13 lung-cancer surgery, Pope Leo sent a video message to the Assisi interfaith gathering marking 40 years since John Paul II's 1986 prayer for peace: 'There is no such thing as a holy war: Only peace is holy.' He condemned the 'revival of war as an instrument of international politics' and religious justifications for war, without naming Iran or the US.

events.label: Trump: 'You'll see Iran in a couple of weeks'
events.description: Not in either researcher's list; found while verifying. At a Lubbock, Texas rally Trump said 'Venezuela, Iran, you'll see Iran in a couple of weeks, if you don't mind', and that Iran was 'defeated militarily, financially and otherwise. And it will all end very soon.' The Washington Examiner read it as a hint that strikes resume after the midterms.

events.label: Vance letter to Rezaei; Trump: 'medical supplies'
events.description: On Oct 28 the WSJ and NYT reported a letter from Vance to SNSC secretary Mohsen Rezaei, passed through Qatari mediators on Sunday (Oct 25). It proposes direct talks with the nuclear programme on the table from the start, and the WSJ said Trump directed it. Trump said he had not and that the letter was about 'medical supplies and various things'. The WaPo later reported that Vance offered to meet Rezaei in person, likely in Doha or Istanbul. Tasnim said Iran had not yet replied.

events.label: US tells allies to prepare for post-midterm strikes
events.description: AP, citing two diplomats, reported on Oct 28 that US officials told Middle East allies to prepare for possible renewed strikes on Iran after the Nov 3 midterms, and for Iranian retaliation against energy and other infrastructure. Gulf officials told MS NOW the first round could come as early as Nov 4 and would be brief but intense. AP said Trump had not made a final decision.

events.label: Hegseth fires Joint Staff planner Lt. Gen. Sylvia
events.description: Hegseth removed Lt. Gen. Brett Sylvia as the Joint Staff's director of strategy, plans and policy (J5). CBS said he was coordinating the Iran battle plan; a War Department official denied he was central to it. A Pentagon official alleged leaks of classified information on Iran and Ukraine and referred the case to the Justice Department; another source cited lack of confidence. He is the second J5 ousted under Hegseth.

events.label: Murphy: post-midterm strike plan 'insane'
events.description: At a Middle East Institute event, Sen. Chris Murphy said that after a briefing on the war plan, 'the plan is insane'. He said it would not achieve its objectives, could hit civilian infrastructure, and would set off 'devastating escalation'. IBTimes dates the event Wednesday Oct 28; the Daily Beast says Thursday.

events.label: Brent at 6-month high; first limpet-mine hit
events.description: The expiring December Brent contract settled up 2.4% at $117.64 on Friday Oct 30, its highest close since late April (January: $113.43). Brent rose 13.6% in October and WTI 15.2%. UKMTO said a small boat attached explosives to a tanker in Hormuz, which maritime sources called the first known successful limpet-mine strike of the war. The IRGC claimed more tankers hit mines; the US called that claim false. The IMO counted 121 attacks and 24 seafarer deaths as of Oct 27.

events.label: Polling avg: 36% support, 57% oppose
events.description: Silver Bulletin's Iran war polling average, updated Oct 30: 36% support and 57% oppose, up from 32/60 at the start of October. The existing Sep 15 event recorded 34/58.

events.label: Trump: Iran war 'going to get wrapped up soon'
events.description: On Kansas City radio KCMO (Fri Oct 30) Trump said the war will be 'wrapped up soon', without a timeline, and 'we need a guarantee there'll never be a nuclear weapon'. At the White House he said Iran keeps seeking talks and the US is in no rush. The WSJ reported that the CENTCOM commander had presented strike options to him. Qatari mediators returned to Tehran the same day.

events.label: Khamenei orders 'geographically unrestricted' response
events.description: After his first publicly disclosed meeting with the armed forces chiefs since the war began, Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei said on Saturday Oct 31 that 'any level or type of threat must be met with an immediate, impactful and geographically unrestricted response'. He ordered the target list updated to cover all 'American-Zionist' assets and said Iran will decide when and how any renewed war ends.

events.label: Rubio: Trump 'hasn't made a decision' on strikes
events.description: Closing the G20 foreign ministers' meeting in Atlanta on Saturday Oct 31, Rubio said Trump 'hasn't made a decision' on resuming strikes, prefers a diplomatic solution ('If there is a diplomatic solution, we would be open to it') and has set no deadline, while not ruling out military action. The meeting produced no joint communiqué.

dropped: Oct 17 fourth 'No Kings' day (researcher B): the protests happened, but the Wikipedia article body never mentions Iran, and Al Jazeera and the Salt Lake Tribune framed them as 'vote early' rallies. No link to the war was found.
Oct 19 Sanders El Paso rally (B): El Paso Matters lists 'the Iran War' only as a talking point and reports no Iran remarks. Nothing to place on the timeline.

Reuters/Ipsos poll, Oct 16-19, 61% oppose (B, low confidence): the release date can't be pinned down. The figures appear only in Iranian state outlets (ABNA, dated Oct 31; Mehr), and CFR (Oct 29) cites a 'mid-October' Reuters/Ipsos poll with matching numbers. Any date would be a guess somewhere between Oct 20 and Oct 29. The Oct 30 polling-average event already covers the trend.

Oct 13 Pope Leo lung surgery (B): confirmed (lobectomy, adenocarcinoma, discharged Oct 17, no further treatment), but not a war event. It is mentioned in the Oct 27 'no holy war' entry and in coverage notes as context for a likely mid-October dip in Vatican and religious_authority output.

Oct 6 'Qatar confirms relaying US-Iran messages' (A): wrong date. Anadolu published Al-Ansari's remarks Tuesday Sep 29 (fetched), and The Peninsula (Sep 30) says 'yesterday'. Merged into the Sep 30 event.

Duplicates merged: Sep 17 Axios interview (A and B); Sep 22 UNGA speech (A and B; Gulf meeting folded in); Sep 26 seven-day-plan rejection; Sep 29 IRGC letter; Oct 5 Los Angeles remark; Oct 8 no-strike pledge; Oct 19 Hegseth visit; Oct 28 Vance letter; Oct 28 Sylvia firing. A's Oct 31 Rubio remarks were split out into their own Oct 31 event, merged with B's.

A's Oct 29 'Trump tells Gulf allies to prepare' was redated to Oct 28, the AP report date. A's attribution of 'another little Epic Fury' to that item was wrong: Trump said it at the Oct 23 Fort Myers rally, now its own event.

Single-event merges: A's Oct 21 FT report and B's NYT/ABC post-midterm-plans item (part of B's Oct 22 entry) became one Oct 21 event. A's Oct 22 IRGC seven-ship claim became context in the Oct 22 Trump event, since the claims are unconfirmed, CENTCOM called the mine claims false, and Trump called them fake.
Sep 18 IRGC 'Trend' tanker strike (A): kept, but redated to Sep 17 (Reuters/BOE Report carried the claim Sep 17).

Unverified details removed from kept events: A Oct 22 'Brent above $117 on Oct 23' (conflicts with Oct 30's $117.64 being the highest close since late April). A Oct 1 'three carriers by end of October' (a US official says the Roosevelt arrives by end of November). A Sep 23 'Cape Dao sunk' and the IMO '85 incidents' count. A Sep 22 CNN 'a lot of momentum' quote. A Sep 23 CBS inspectors line and White House 'evil country' quote. A Oct 8 'Brent +5% to $105.5'. A Oct 8 Oct 21 second sanctions round and rial rate. A Oct 19 Trump endorsement of Netanyahu (Oct 18). A Oct 29 CNN '96 hours' detail. A Oct 31 Araghchi 'positive step' quote. A Sep 30 Araghchi Oct 8 'within days' quote. B Sep 24 Thune quote and 'last vote before midterms'. B Sep 17 'June margin 17 points' and '47% less safe'. B Oct 5 Desmond/Kiley reactions. B Oct 6 Rubio Athens remark.
verify_note: Verified 2026-10-31 by a research workflow (two researchers, one verifier); each kept event confirmed by a fresh search or by opening a source.
